# Purpose and endpoint

Start from **what reproducible research means**, note where definitions diverge (including qualitative work), then teach everyday **workflows**: durable project folder, documentation, versioning, sharing boundaries, responsible AI use.

Students organise a folder and write documentation for **their own PhD project**, then transfer text into the course Swedish Research Council DMP template.

**Working definition ([The Turing Way](https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/overview/overview-definitions/)):** work that can be independently recreated from the **same data and the same analysis**. Caveats: fields swap *reproducible* / *replicable*; for much qualitative work the practical aim is *auditability* ([Keele KORSA](https://www.keele.ac.uk/korsa/qualitative/reproducibilityreplication/)). KI does not define the term; it requires documentation and openness so research can be followed, interpreted, and reproduced ([Riktlinjer](https://medarbetare.ki.se/media/99275/download) §§6–7; [documentation guidelines](https://staff.ki.se/research-support/research-data-management/plan-your-research-data-management/guidelines-for-research-documentation-and-data-management)).

**5-year test:** someone returning in five years can understand what was done and which decisions were made. (KI retention is ≥10 years.)

| Block | Time | Day 1 | Day 2 |
|-------|------|-------|-------|
| Morning | 09:00–12:00 | Self-study | Self-study |
| Afternoon | 13:00–16:00 | Hybrid: room **Future** + [Zoom](https://ki-se.zoom.us/j/68142022512) | Zoom only (same link) |

# Learning outcomes

By the end of the two days, the student can:

1. **Explain** the Turing Way definition, note where definitions diverge (including qualitative auditability), and relate that to KI’s research and documentation guidelines.
2. **Structure** a durable project folder and its documentation (README, decision log, naming and versioning) so the project passes the 5-year test.
3. **Track** changes and decisions in a form humans and tools can both read, and justify which versioning approach fits their project.
4. **Draft** SRC DMP answers on **documentation**, **data description**, **data quality**, **storage**, **security**, and **who is responsible**.
5. **Judge** what can be shared, what must stay protected, and how to use KI-supported AI (Copilot-first) responsibly — with disclosure and verification.

# Standing rules (every block)

- **Versioning:** prefer one shared master in **Office Online** on KI Teams/SharePoint, with regular downloads named per KI §6.1. Google Docs fine for shared text. Dated copies + decision log OK. Git allowed if already used; do not teach Git.
- **AI:** prefer Microsoft Copilot; never put personal/patient/sensitive research data in prompts; keep prompt + output; verify and edit; disclose to the team.
- **TBL close:** every application ends with **2–3 team findings on the shared board + whole-group discussion** (not classic simultaneous report). **Full** 5-year rubric only in Day 1 App 1 and Day 2 peer critique.
- **DMP:** after each major activity, paste under the exact SRC questions in the map below. Mark text as *draft* for the course assignment.
- Synthetic / fictional data only in examples.

## Day 1 App 1 — planted-violation detail (facilitators only)

**Do not share this section with students.** Material: two view-only Google Drive folders under [Exercise 1](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1vQgA7VL_Bw2BN6U4PwI0Mk94ZPkJ2hpG). Mapping for facilitators only: `bednet-survey-transnzoia` = good; `bednet-study` = poor. Teams use the student [5-year rubric](../canvas/pages/five-year-rubric.md) from the start. About 25 minutes to compare, then post **2–3 findings** on the shared board (Future + Zoom), naming the folder and a rubric criterion. Lead a whole-group discussion of those posts (D049).

### The fictional study

*Bednet availability and usage in Trans-Nzoia County, Kenya*: a small mixed-methods study, a household survey (~20 synthetic responses) plus key-informant interviews. Fictional researchers: Jane Wanjiru (JW) and David Otieno (DO), Kitale; Anna Lindqvist (AL), KI collaborator. All names, data, and reference numbers are invented. The survey data is generated by a seeded script.

### The "good" folder

```
bednet-survey-transnzoia/
  README            (overview; naming + versioning convention; pointers to material on approved storage)
  DECISIONS         (dated log, 5 entries)
  data/       survey-responses_2024-03-10.csv   (raw, immutable; date = collection date)
  doc/        protocol                          (Doc with version table inside)
              data-dictionary                   (Sheet: variable-level metadata)
              interview-guide                   (Doc with version table inside)
              interview-log                     (Sheet: live tracking, incl. planned + declined rows)
  analysis/   clean-survey-data.R               (defines the cleaning function; every correction in code)
              analysis.R                        (sources it, cleans raw in memory, writes results)
  results/    table1-descriptives.csv           (the only generated file; GEP: analysis outputs go in results)
```

Conventions it models (stated in its README):

- Plain content-based names (GEP), no version or status suffixes. Dates only where the date is content (collection date). Agreed early, applied consistently (KI guidelines, Active data).
- Versioning: a version table inside each governed document per the KI guidelines. A decision log for why things changed.
- No saved intermediates: the cleaning function recreates the analysis-ready data in every run, and `results/` holds only generated tables (GEP: record all the steps).
- Prose as Google Docs, tables as Sheets (working formats); data as CSV and scripts as plain text (durable formats).
- Sensitive material (recordings, transcripts, signed consents) on KI-approved storage with regulated access; the folder holds pointers and the tracking log only (Riktlinjer §7).
- Interview log lives in `doc/`, not `data/`: it is a living process document, not immutable collected data. It tracks planned, completed, and declined interviews (auditability: who is missing shapes what the data can say).

### The "poor" folder: planted violations

Folder name on Drive: **`bednet-study`**. File-for-file mirror of the good one, with 6 planted violations. Mapping: README (stale), DECISIONS → `notes.docx` (undated diary), the raw CSV → `data.xlsx` (silently edited), the two scripts → `analysis_final.R` (decoy), the generated table → `results_tables.docx` (hand-made), the interview log kept but stripped of its ids; the data dictionary is absent, which leaves the red rows and the 99-codes meaningless. Everything else (protocol, interview guide, the log's content) is fine. Numbers do not match: `data.xlsx` has 19 rows with 2 marked red; the manuscript (dated 2024-03-28) says n = 18, written when one red row was still in; results say n = 17. In `notes.docx` there is a decision log to remove two patients, but highlighting exclusions in red in the data file leads to several errors downstream.

| # | Planted how | Violates | Reading link |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `data/data.xlsx`: unclear whether raw or already edited (it is edited: one household silently lost, typos silently fixed). No untouched raw version anywhere. | Keep raw data untouched, clearly identified as raw | GEP [Save the raw data](https://carpentries-lab.github.io/good-enough-practices/aio.html#save-the-raw-data); KI Guidelines for research §6 |
| 2 | `analysis/analysis_final.R` looks credible but reads `C:/Users/dotieno/Desktop/data_v2.xlsx` — a path and file that exist nowhere. The comment "fixed the two typos in Excel first" documents hand-editing. The script cannot run. | Record every processing step, in runnable code with portable paths | GEP [Record all the steps](https://carpentries-lab.github.io/good-enough-practices/aio.html#record-all-the-steps-used-to-process-data) |
| 3 | Two rows in `data.xlsx` are red with no legend. `doc/notes.docx` holds the only explanation, drowned among per-diem and motorbike entries: "2024-03-20: Marked potential exclusions in red" (no author) and "2024-04-05: Decision by group to exclude the red surveys". The exclusion list exists only as cell colour, which dies on any export. Hence n = 19 vs 18 vs 17 across data, manuscript, and results. | Exclusions as documented data (a variable), not formatting; decisions with author and rationale | GEP [Create analysis-friendly data](https://carpentries-lab.github.io/good-enough-practices/aio.html#create-analysis-friendly-data); KI guidelines, Active data |
| 4 | `README.docx` is week-1 text: names two files that no longer exist, promises a decision log that was never kept. | README as living overview | GEP [Create an overview](https://carpentries-lab.github.io/good-enough-practices/aio.html#create-an-overview-of-your-project); 5-year test |
| 5 | `doc/interview-log.xlsx` exists and is well maintained — but informants appear by first name only, with no id column and no consent column. Nothing links Grace to her transcript file, and nothing can tell you whether any interviewed person is also a surveyed household (the good log's KII ids are exactly what makes those links possible). The fifth row ("sub-county officer, brief chat at market") is the only trace of that conversation anywhere. | Unique identifiers across files; consent tracking | GEP [Multiple tables, unique identifiers](https://carpentries-lab.github.io/good-enough-practices/aio.html#use-multiple-tables-as-necessary-and-use-a-unique-identifier-for-every-record); [Keele KORSA](https://www.keele.ac.uk/korsa/qualitative/reproducibilityreplication/) (auditability) |
| 6 | The recording of the Grace interview travelled on a USB stick and was lost in transit (notes, 2024-03-17). The transcript reappears three weeks later, retyped from memory (notes, 2024-04-08), as `doc/interview_Grace-M.docx` — participant name in the filename, in the shared folder. The retyped transcript quietly replaces a primary source with recollection. | No sensitive data on portable media; incidents are reported; no personal data in the open; primary data is not reconstructed from memory | KI guidelines, Storage sharing and archiving; Riktlinjer §7 |

Deliberately fine, to keep the folder credible: the protocol and interview guide are decent documents matching the study as conducted (their only quiet gap: no version tables), the interview log is genuinely maintained, and the folder skeleton itself is correct. The teaching point is that structure alone does not make a project reproducible.

### Expected team findings and facilitation

Will likely find 4 quickly (README vs actual contents). 1, 2, and 6 require reading files closely; 3 and 5 require cross-referencing several files, and the full n = 19/18/17 reconstruction is a stretch goal — praise any team that gets there. Prompts:

- If a team posts only surface findings: "Could you redo their analysis five years from now? What exactly stops you? Which rubric question does that hit?"
- If a team never opens the rubric: "Try Decision traceability or Orientability on both folders — where does each answer live?"
- Discussion prompt on the good folder: "Why is the interview log in `doc/` and not `data/`?" (living document vs immutable data; Separation of concerns).
- Discussion prompt on versioning: "This team versions through version tables + the decision log. What else could they have chosen, and when would that be better?" Talking points: filename versioning with dated copies (KI name parts), git if already used.

Together the six violations span the assigned Day 1 readings, both KI documents, and both quantitative and qualitative studies.

## Day 1 App 2 — facilitator cues

Student steps: [`canvas/pages/day-1-afternoon.md`](../canvas/pages/day-1-afternoon.md) (Exercise 2). Each student builds or improves a folder + README for **one study in their own PhD** (no shared vignette). Manual drafting is fine. Copilot is allowed under the morning AI rules.

**Paste into SRC**: both **data description** prompts and **documentation** (map below).

**Light within-team check only**: about 2–3 minutes each. Ask “Could a colleague find their way around?” and “What would make it easier?” Owner notes improvements before Day 2. Do **not** walk the full 5-year rubric here. Stay in TBL teams. Same shared board for Future + Zoom.

Then each team posts **2–3 findings** (patterns or stuck points, e.g. no place for exclusions yet) and join whole-group discussion.

Prompts:

- If someone jumps to ChatGPT or similar: restate the morning AI block (Copilot-first; no sensitive data; keep prompt + output; verify; disclose).
- If the light check stalls on praise: “Point at one file a future colleague would open first. Is that named in the README?”
- If DMP text floats free of the folder: “Which folder path or README sentence does this draft answer?”
- Keep versioning light. Day 2 covers Office Online, §6.1 naming, and dated copies.

Closing (15:45): each person names one improvement before Day 2 and how it supports the Turing Way definition or auditability.

# Session → SRC DMP map

Template: [`Swedish_Research_Council_Template__v5.docx`](../Swedish_Research_Council_Template__v5.docx). Only these six areas.

| When | Area | SRC template question |
|------|------|------------------------|
| Day 1 | Data description | *How will data be collected, created or reused?* |
| Day 1 | Data description | *What types of data… format and amount/volume?* |
| Day 1 | Documentation | *How will the material be documented and described…?* |
| Day 2 | Documentation | *How will the material be documented and described…?* (update with readable history / versioning) |
| Day 2 | Data quality | *How will data quality be safeguarded and documented…?* |
| Day 2 | Storage | *How is storage and backup… safeguarded during the research process?* |
| Day 2 | Security | *How is data security and controlled access… safeguarded…?* |
| Day 2 | Who is responsible | *Who is responsible for data management… during and after the project?* |

# Scope

**In scope:** definition + limits; folder, documentation, versioning, sharing boundaries, responsible AI; the six DMP areas above.

**Out of scope:** programming, statistics, pipelines, containers; Git beyond a short option (see K8F6106); data collection protocol (assignment component 2); other SRC questions (legal, ethics, accessibility, long-term storage, software, DOI, costs); metascience lecture; shared case vignette; minute-level scripts; new TBL hosting.
